text: dsh-intent-recognition 是面向 DSH Web 的意图识别与路由插件。它在侧边栏和设置页提供管理界面，并为运行中的服务注册可供 agent 调用的识别工具，也开放给其他插件的 Cordis 服务接口。它可按规则、向量召回、Jev、微调模型和 LLM 后备层逐步识别意图，管理场景、意图、模型和服务，并把匹配结果路由到工作流、子 agent 或 Cordis 服务。适合需要将自然语言请求分类并交给既有业务流程的 DSH 部署。基础版使用本地 JSON 存储；向量检索需配置 PostgreSQL 与 pgvector。

dsh-intent-recognition classifies DSH requests and routes matches to workflows, subagents, or Cordis services. It provides a management panel and agent tools. Rules, vector retrieval, Jev, fine-tuned models, and an LLM can power recognition; basic mode stores data locally.

dsh-intent-recognition 的功能「分层意图识别」：服务按配置运行规则、向量召回、Jev、微调模型和 LLM 后备识别，并返回匹配结果及各层 trace。通过运行中的服务工具或 Cordis 接口提交请求。
dsh-intent-recognition 的功能「服务工具与路由」：每个运行中的服务可注册一个 intent_recognize 工具，识别后可按路由配置执行工作流、子 agent 或 Cordis 服务。工具随服务停止或删除而撤销。
dsh-intent-recognition 的功能「场景管理界面」：在侧边栏主面板和设置区打开管理界面，配置场景、意图、模型及服务，并通过管理 API 与插件交互。
dsh-intent-recognition 的基础版不含向量检索；启用层 2 和向量实验室需切换到 PostgreSQL + pgvector 高级版。

A DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin: five-layer intent recognition pipeline + scenario/intent management UI + dual-edition storage (basic = zero-config local file, advanced = PostgreSQL + pgvector) + distributable API services + DSH-native routing (agent tools / workflows / subagents / Cordis services).

dsh-intent-recognition README · dsh-intent-recognition：**Every layer can be toggled off per service** — disabled layers are skipped entirely.

dsh-intent-recognition README · Control plane + data plane：- **Control plane (management UI)**: the **Intent Recognition** sidebar panel (same level as the Plugins entry; pin/unpin from the sidebar's More menu), plus a Settings → Intent Recognition section — both render the same management UI. Tooling only; it never joins the conversation.
- **Data plane (consumable services)**: a running service can be consumed two ways:

dsh-intent-recognition README · Control plane + data plane：| Channel | Notes | Best for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Agent tool** (recommended) | each running service registers `intent_recognize_<service-slug>`; high-confidence hits execute the route inside the tool | DSH main agent routing user turns |
| **Cordis service** | `ctx.intentRecognition.predict(service, query, context)` for other plugins | programmatic integration |

dsh-intent-recognition README · Features：- **Zero-config start**: the basic edition (local file storage) is the default — install and build intents, models and services without any database. Upgrade to the advanced edition in-page whenever you need vector retrieval; existing data migrates automatically.
- **Intent management**: per-scenario intent catalog (name/code/description/examples/keywords/blacklist/whitelist/route config), Excel import (merge/replace) & export, one-click embedding rebuild (advanced).
- **Model configuration**: embedding, Jev, fine-tuned and LLM models are all page-configured (OpenAI-compatible or plain http JSON endpoints), with connectivity tests.
- **Service management**: per-scenario API services, independent switches & parameters per layer, services can **run / stop / delete / copy**; per-service API keys; built-in test console and call logs.
- **Vector lab** (advanced): a dedicated tab for layer-2 recall debugging — recall tests (type a question, see per-chunk scores and the aggregated intent candidate set, optionally inheriting a service's threshold/TopK), chunk browsing (example text / dims / building model / timestamp, with single-chunk delete), and

dsh-intent-recognition README · Features：Tabs follow the order of use: **Intents → Models → Services → Vector (advanced) → Database**. Until the first service exists, a three-step onboarding strip sits on top of the page; in the basic edition the Vector tab carries a 🔒 and opens an upgrade explainer.

text: dsh-intent-recognition README · Editions: basic vs advanced：Since v0.7.0 the plugin ships two storage editions; a banner on first open explains which one is active:

dsh-intent-recognition README · Editions: basic vs advanced：| | Basic (default) | Advanced |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Storage | Local JSON file (next to the connection config, e.g. `data.json`) | PostgreSQL + pgvector |
| Database required | No — zero config | Yes (page-configured, instant effect) |
| L1 rules / L3 Jev / L4 fine-tuned / L5 LLM | ✅ | ✅ |
| L2 vector retrieval, vector lab, embedding rebuild | ❌ (tab shows 🔒; L2 is skipped at runtime with a trace note) | ✅ |
| Best for | trying things out, rule-driven catalogs | large intent libraries, diverse phrasings, semantic recall |

dsh-intent-recognition README · Editions: basic vs advanced：- **Upgrade**: fill in the PostgreSQL connection on the Database tab and "Test & Save". With "Migrate local data" on (default), existing scenarios/intents/models/services are copied into the database **keeping ids and API keys**, so agent tools and API callers notice nothing. Re-migration is idempotent (existing rows are skipped). Rebuild embeddings afterwards to enable L2.
- **Downgrade**: "Switch back to basic" on the Database tab returns storage to the local file — **local data stays exactly as it was before the upgrade** (rows created in advanced are not written back), and the connection config is kept for the next upgrade.
- **Edition resolution** (at boot): explicit basic choice > page-saved connection > patch `databaseUrl` (only if reachable) > basic fallback. The plugin always loads and the panel always opens.

dsh-intent-recognition README · Database connection (advanced edition)：The "Intent Recognition → Database" tab manages the edition and the advanced connection: a "Storage edition" card on top shows the current edition, the local data file path, and per-table row counts. In the advanced edition it offers a structured form (host/port/database/user/password/SSL) or a raw DSN, **Test connection** (also probes pgvector availability), **Test & Save** (persists + hot-swaps storage without any restart), **Clear page config** (fall back to the patch DSN or basic), **Switch back to basic**, and **Migrate local data into this database** (available whenever local rows exist).

dsh-intent-recognition README · Database connection (advanced edition)：While the database is unreachable (advanced edition), a red banner at the top of the panel guides you to the Database tab; saving hot-swaps storage and takes effect immediately:

| Disconnected banner | Database tab (connected) |
| --- | --- |
|  |  |

dsh-intent-recognition README · Database connection (advanced edition)：- **Priority**: explicit basic choice > page-saved DSN > `cordis.patch.yml` `databaseUrl` (only counts when reachable) > basic fallback. An unreachable page-saved DSN never silently falls back to basic (that would split your data) — the panel still opens, management routes answer 503, and you recover by fixing the connection or explicitly switching back to basic.
- **Persistence**: `%APPDATA%/dsh-intent-recognition/` (Windows), `~/Library/Application Support/dsh-intent-recognition/` (macOS), `~/.config/dsh-intent-recognition/` (Linux); override with the `DSH_INTENT_RECOGNITION_CONFIG` env var. Inside: `connection.json` (advanced DSN; password masked as `***` in API responses, submitting `***` keeps the stored one), `data.json` (basic-edition data), `storage.json` (explicit basic marker). All files are mode 0600.
- **pgvector**: with `autoMigrate` on, a successful save runs `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector` plus schema migration automatically; the test button warns beforehand when the target lacks pgvector. A database without pgvector can be connected, but L2 stays unavailable (the page says so).
- **Databa

dsh-intent-recognition README · Plugin configuration：| Field | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `databaseUrl` | `postgres://postgres:postgres@127.0.0.1:5432/dsh_intent` | Advanced-edition fallback DSN (page-saved config wins; only counts when reachable, otherwise basic edition); pgvector must be available |
| `embeddingDim` | `1024` | Must match the configured embedding model; changing it requires an embedding rebuild |
| `autoMigrate` | `true` | Create tables/indexes on load (HNSW cosine index, pgvector ≥ 0.5) |
| `adminToken` | `''` | Bearer token protecting the management API; empty = DSH loopback only |
| `registerTool` | `true` | Register one `intent_recognize_<slug>` tool per running service |
| `contributePrompt` | `true` | Inject a system-prompt section listing available intent services |

dsh-intent-recognition README · Intent routes：| Route type | Config | Behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `none` | — | Return the recognition result only |
| `workflow` | target (run name) + workflow script | Starts a DSH workflow run; the script orchestrates freely (call subagents, tools, other plugins) |
| `subagent` | target = **agent preset id** | Spawns a subagent with that preset to handle the query (`provider: spawn`, result returned to caller) |
| `service` | target = `serviceName.method` | Calls a method of another Cordis service in the host (capability provided by another plugin) |

dsh-intent-recognition README · Execution policy (`route_mode`)：- **auto (default)**: deterministic hits (L1 / L3 / L4) **execute the route inside the tool** — the cheap deterministic path actually lands; L5 (LLM fallback) hits only return the route as a suggestion for the main agent.
- **suggest**: never executes; the route is returned to the caller (agent or HTTP client).

Results carry `route` when configured; after execution they also carry `route_result` (`ok / value / error`).
dsh-intent-recognition README · Workflow scripts：With route type `workflow`, write the script directly in the intent editor (a collapsible full guide is built into the page). The script receives:

dsh-intent-recognition README · Workflow scripts：| Variable | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `args.query` | raw user input |
| `args.intent` | matched intent code |
| `args.confidence` | 0–1 |
| `args.matched_layer` | `l1`–`l5` |
| `args.slots` | slots extracted by L5 |
| `args.context` | caller-provided context array |
| `agent(prompt)` | spawn a subagent inside the script |
| `meta` | run metadata (`meta.name` = route target) |
dsh-intent-recognition README · Plugging downstream capabilities into DSH：The whole system treats DSH as the backbone — intent routing and downstream agents/workflows all attach as plugins:

dsh-intent-recognition README · Plugging downstream capabilities into DSH：1. **Workflows**: scripts live in the intent's route config and travel with the catalog via Excel import/export ("workflow script" column). Reuse capabilities via `agent()` or route type `service`.
2. **Subagents**: ship downstream capabilities as **agent preset** plugins (see `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset`); put the preset id in the route target.
3. **Cordis services**: a downstream plugin does `ctx.reflect.provide('xxxService', ...)` in `apply`; set the route target to `xxxService.methodName`. The method is called as `(result, exec)` where `result` carries query/intent/confidence/slots.

dsh-intent-recognition README · Using services in the chat window (Agent tools)：Once a service is **running**, the plugin registers a chat tool `intent_recognize_<slug>` with DSH (slug derived from the service name; revoked automatically when the service stops). From then on, just ask in any conversation — the main agent calls the tool when relevant and the route config dispatches to workflows / subagents / Cordis services. You can also invoke it explicitly, e.g. "use intent_recognize_bank_router to check: I want to transfer money".

text: dsh-intent-recognition README · Jev extra-config auto-generation (systemone wire format)：The Jev model dialog offers two **extra-config generators**; pick a scenario whose intents are configured, then choose:

dsh-intent-recognition README · Jev extra-config auto-generation (systemone wire format)：- **AI generation**: calls a configured LLM (add one under model configuration first; if none is configured or the call fails, the error is surfaced — use the rule template instead). The full intent descriptions (definition / inclusion signals / exclusion rules / boundary distinctions, with examples) are passed to the model verbatim, and the prompt demands faithful preservation of those rules.
- **Rule template**: deterministic, no LLM required — embeds each intent's full description into `instructions` with generic five-band scoring criteria.

dsh-intent-recognition README · Jev extra-config auto-generation (systemone wire format)：Both generate **all three judgment modes at once** (`modes.score` / `modes.choice` / `modes.noul`). Since v0.6.0 each mode carries **a single question named `intent_recognition`** that judges every candidate intent in one call:

dsh-intent-recognition README · Jev extra-config auto-generation (systemone wire format)：| Mode | type | criteria | answer | score mapping |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| score | `score` | array of per-intent decision descriptions, plus `intent_order` (intent codes aligned 1:1 with criteria) | score array (in `intent_order` order) or `{code: score}` object | array indexes map via `intent_order` |
| choice | `choice` | `{intent name: decision description}` object | one intent name | chosen = 1, others = 0 |
| noul | `noul` | — (`map` binds “是”/“否” to the two intent codes) | “是”/“否” | per `map`: hit = 1, other = 0 |

dsh-intent-recognition README · Jev extra-config auto-generation (systemone wire format)：> **noul is only generated for exactly-2-intent scenarios** — yes/no cannot cover more; don't pick noul as the layer-3 mode otherwise.

**Which mode runs is chosen per service**: the service editor's layer 3 has a "judgment mode" dropdown (score/choice/noul, default score); layer 3 then sends the corresponding `modes.<mode>` question. Legacy extra configs (per-intent `modes` questions, or a single top-level `questions`) keep working — layer 3 falls back to per-intent calls.

dsh-intent-recognition README · Jev extra-config auto-generation (systemone wire format)：Layer-3 thresholds decide the outcome: **top score ≥ high threshold** → direct hit (skips L4/L5); **[mid, high)** → compressed candidates go to L4 arbitration; **below mid** → L5 fallback. The result is a draft — review it in the extra-config field before saving.

A Jev model with this extra config (`api_style=http`) switches layer 3 to the systemone wire format:

dsh-intent-recognition README · Jev extra-config auto-generation (systemone wire format)：Score answers may be an array aligned with `intent_order`, a `{scores|values|results: [...]}` wrapper, or a `{code: score}` object; choice answers are an intent name (「」 quotes, codes, case and containment tolerant); noul answers are “是”/“否” mapped via the question's `map`. All three modes also accept object answers like `{choice: "name", confidence: 1, probabilities: {name: p}}` — `probabilities` maps are scored directly, otherwise the `choice`/`answer`/`value` label field is matched. Legacy per-intent answers `{"answers": {"<intent code>": ...}}` keep working: numbers, booleans, `"是"/"否"/"true"` strings, or `{score|probability|confidence}` objects.

dsh-intent-recognition README · Layer-2 retrieval transparency：The layer-2 "confidence threshold (min similarity)" (`minScore`) in the service editor is the slice filter — recalled chunks below it never become candidates. Test traces now expose it: layer 2 carries `minScore` / `topK` / `chunks` (every raw recalled slice with its score and pass/fail) / `candidates` (post-aggregation), so "recalled but not adopted" is directly attributable to threshold filtering vs aggregation truncation; layer 3 traces carry the judgment `mode`.

dsh-intent-recognition README · Vector lab (layer-2 debugging)：> Advanced-edition feature (requires pgvector). In the basic edition the tab shows 🔒 with an upgrade explainer; available after upgrading and rebuilding embeddings.

The **Vector Lab** tab answers "why was recall wrong for this question":

dsh-intent-recognition README · Vector lab (layer-2 debugging)：1. **Recall test**: pick a scenario, type any question, and the plugin replays the engine's real layer-2 logic (same `searchSimilar`, per-intent best chunk, minScore filter, TopK truncation). Optionally reference a service to inherit its embedding model and layer-2 threshold/TopK, or pick a model and tweak the threshold ad hoc. Two result tables: the **intent aggregation** (what layer 2 would actually emit downstream) and the **raw chunk hits** (every recalled slice with its score).
2. **Chunk browser**: all embedding slices of a scenario (example text, owning intent, dims, building model, build time), filterable by intent, paginated, with per-chunk delete for stale slices.
3. **Coverage overview**: per-scenario intent/example/chunk counts, coverage gaps, the models that built the slices, last rebuild time, and in-place rebuild with a chosen model.

dsh-intent-recognition README · Vector lab (layer-2 debugging)：Slices carry model provenance (`model_id`); after switching embedding models or editing examples, rebuild — otherwise old and new slices live in incompatible vector spaces.

dsh-intent-recognition README · Excel template：Header row: `Name | Code | Description | Examples | Keywords | Blacklist | Whitelist | Route Type | Route Target | Workflow Script`. Multi-values inside examples are newline-separated, others use `、`; route type is `none / workflow / subagent / service` (a target or script without a type infers `workflow`). The exported file is the template.
